methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a well-matched observational design to compare the immune/stromal microenvironment of primary PDAC (27 samples) versus liver metastases (26 samples) using multiplex IHC/IF, spatial analysis, and single-cell mass cytometry. Methods provide concrete inclusion/exclusion constraints (e.g., metastatic-biopsy patients excluded if previously treated with anti–PD-1/PD-L1; off treatment at biopsy; defined collection windows) and quality control (pathologist review of H&E to confirm tumor and sample quality, exclusion of unsuitable regions). The statistical plan is described at a high level (Mann–Whitney/Wilcoxon for two-group comparisons, two-way ANOVA with multiple-comparison corrections), and spatial analyses specify algorithms and seeds for reproducibility. Limitations include observational confounding (different clinical contexts for resection vs metastatic biopsy) and no explicit power calculation for the multi-marker, multi-assay comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual observational study comparing cohorts of primary and metastatic PDAC tissues, which fits Oxford LoE 2b in the rubric’s mapping for observational designs. The clinical relevance is high because metastatic PDAC is the dominant lethal setting and the manuscript directly addresses the translational gap that most immune-target selection is derived from primary tumors. Findings such as reduced T-cell infiltration in liver metastases and increased CD68+ macrophage abundance provide a rationale for revisiting immunotherapy strategies and target prioritization in metastatic disease. However, endpoints are tissue/immune-feature based rather than patient outcomes or therapeutic response, so the work informs strategy rather than immediately changing practice.

reporting_quality.justification: For a human observational tissue-comparison study, STROBE is the most applicable checklist, and the manuscript reports key cohort context (collection years, clinical trial identifiers for metastatic biopsies, key exclusion criteria) and laboratory protocols for staining, imaging, and quantification. Analytical reproducibility is supported by explicit software versions, defined segmentation parameters, and named spatial/community-detection methods with fixed seeds. Some STROBE items are only partially visible in the normalized text, including how missing data and multiple testing across many markers were handled and whether analyses were pre-specified. Data and code deposition are not clearly stated (no visible public repositories for CyTOF/mIHC outputs or analysis scripts), suggesting limited availability.

novelty_literature.justification: The work’s novelty is in a protein-level, spatially informed comparison of primary versus metastatic PDAC microenvironments across a reasonably sized cohort using multiplex imaging and CyTOF, emphasizing metastatic-specific immune communities. The specific observation set (reduced T cells/fibroblasts/collagen in liver metastases with increased CD68+/CCR2 features and checkpoint receptor coexpression on T cells) provides a useful, clinically oriented dataset. Similar themes about PDAC immune exclusion and macrophage dominance have been reported previously, so the conceptual novelty is moderate rather than high. The contribution is best viewed as a high-quality, multi-modal characterization that strengthens and refines prior hypotheses.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with a focused question (primary vs metastatic PDAC immune/stromal features) and a methods section that provides concrete technical detail for multiplex staining, imaging, and downstream quantification. The abstract is specific about the modalities used (mIHC, spatial analysis, CyTOF) and the main biological contrasts between sites, aligning well with the results narrative. Limitations and clinical implications are discussed with appropriate restraint and connected to prior immunotherapy trial context. Because figure visuals are not present in the normalized corpus, interpretation depends on captions and method clarity, which are generally sufficient.

key_strengths: Multi-modal tissue profiling (mIHC/IF with spatial analysis plus CyTOF) directly comparing primary PDAC to liver metastases in human samples
Clear cohort context and practical exclusion criteria for metastatic biopsies (including prior checkpoint exposure), improving interpretability
Reproducible analysis detail with software versions, segmentation parameters, and specified spatial/community algorithms
key_concerns: Observational comparisons are vulnerable to confounding from differing clinical settings (resection primary tumors vs metastatic biopsies) and treatment histories
Multiplicity and pre-specification of hypotheses across many markers/modalities are not clearly articulated in the normalized text
No explicit power/sample-size justification and limited linkage to clinical outcomes or treatment response
Data and code availability statements are not clearly present, limiting independent reanalysis
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a solid, well-reported observational characterization with clear translational motivation; it is likely suitable for a tier-3 venue with minor revisions focused on statistical/multiplicity clarity and reproducibility disclosures.
